learningObjectives.title: Crude oil, fractional distillation and hydrocarbons
The Earth's atmosphere and climate change

questions.q: What is crude oil?
questions.explain: Crude oil is a finite, non-renewable mixture made up mostly of hydrocarbons.

questions.q: What is the general formula for the alkanes?
questions.explain: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n+2.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of methane, the first alkane?
questions.explain: Methane has one carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms, giving CH4.

questions.q: Fractional distillation separates crude oil into fractions according to differences in their:
questions.explain: Fractions separate because different-sized hydrocarbon molecules have different boiling points.

questions.q: As hydrocarbon molecules in crude oil become larger, what happens to their properties?
options: Their boiling point increases and they become more viscous
questions.explain: Longer hydrocarbon chains have stronger intermolecular forces, so higher boiling points and greater viscosity.

questions.q: Cracking a large hydrocarbon molecule produces which of the following?
questions.explain: Cracking breaks large molecules into more useful shorter alkanes and reactive alkenes.

questions.q: Cracking one molecule of decane (C10H22) produces one molecule of octane (C8H18) and one other molecule. What is the other molecule?
questions.explain: The atoms must balance: C10H22 gives C8H18 plus C2H4 (ethene).

questions.q: What are the products of the complete combustion of a hydrocarbon fuel?
questions.explain: With plenty of oxygen, hydrocarbons burn completely to form carbon dioxide and water.

questions.q: Incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon can produce which toxic gas?
questions.explain: A limited oxygen supply produces the toxic gas carbon monoxide instead of carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Why is carbon monoxide dangerous to humans?
options: It binds to haemoglobin, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen
It dissolves in rain to form an acid
It is highly explosive at room temperature
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide bonds to haemoglobin in red blood cells, preventing them from carrying oxygen.

questions.q: Which pollutant, formed from sulfur impurities in fuels, is a major cause of acid rain?
questions.explain: Sulfur impurities burn to form sulfur dioxide, which dissolves in rain to make it acidic.

questions.q: How are oxides of nitrogen (NOx) produced inside a car engine?
options: Nitrogen and oxygen from the air react together at the high temperatures
Sulfur impurities in the fuel burn
Nitrogen dissolves in water in the engine
questions.explain: The high temperatures in engines make nitrogen and oxygen from the air react to form oxides of nitrogen.

questions.q: Balance the equation: CH4 + ?O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O. What is the coefficient of O2?
questions.explain: Two O2 molecules supply the four oxygen atoms needed for one CO2 and two H2O.

questions.q: Approximately what percentage of today's atmosphere is nitrogen?
questions.explain: Nitrogen makes up about four-fifths (roughly 78%) of the modern atmosphere.

questions.q: Approximately what percentage of today's atmosphere is oxygen?
questions.explain: Oxygen makes up about one-fifth (roughly 21%) of the modern atmosphere.

questions.q: Which gas is thought to have made up most of the Earth's early atmosphere, released by intense volcanic activity?
questions.explain: The early atmosphere is thought to have been mainly carbon dioxide with little or no oxygen.

questions.q: Which process is mainly responsible for the increase in oxygen in the atmosphere over billions of years?
questions.explain: Algae and later plants released oxygen through photosynthesis, gradually building up atmospheric oxygen.

questions.q: Which of these gases is a greenhouse gas?
questions.explain: Methane, along with carbon dioxide and water vapour, is a greenhouse gas that absorbs thermal radiation.

questions.q: Global cattle farming and rice-paddy agriculture have expanded greatly. Which greenhouse gas would you expect this to increase?
questions.explain: Livestock and rice paddies release methane, a greenhouse gas, so its levels rise with these activities.

questions.q: Records show atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration and average global temperature have both risen over the same period. This is best described as:
options: A correlation between carbon dioxide and temperature
Proof that temperature has no link to carbon dioxide
Evidence of falling greenhouse gas levels
questions.explain: Two variables changing together shows a correlation, which supports links between CO2 and warming.
